facts.heading: General anxiety level
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time. This anxiety got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September.

facts.heading: Work role change
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school. She has taught there for 11 years.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school. I've taught here for 11 years and I've loved it.

facts.heading: Pressure to step up
facts.content: The head asked Hannah to step up when the deputy left.
facts.evidence: And then the head asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of incompetence
facts.content: Hannah worries that people think she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety manifestation
facts.content: Hannah's chest tightens and she rehearses meetings in her head on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing potential criticism
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say.
facts.evidence: I rehearse every possible question someone might ask and what I would say and what they would think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth.

facts.heading: Fear of being incompetent
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is incapable of reading.
facts.evidence: That they gave the job to a nice ear for a teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: No external feedback
facts.content: No one has said anything that suggests these negative thoughts.
facts.evidence: Has anyone said anything that suggests that? No, that's the strange thing. Nobody has.

facts.heading: Rewriting emails repeatedly
facts.content: Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times.
facts.evidence: Last week, I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of being perceived as stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Governor's treatment
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves has been kind to Hannah.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind.

facts.heading: Feeling of deception
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about her capability.
facts.evidence: That makes it worse somehow, because I feel like I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Identity comparison
facts.content: Hannah compares her current job to her mother's career.
facts.evidence: I can't help comparing. Everything I do, I think would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's career status
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a head teacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a head teacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother's legacy
facts.content: People in the village still praise Hannah's mother's work.
facts.evidence: Everyone in the village still stops me, say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Mother's retirement
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.

facts.heading: Mother's support
facts.content: Hannah's mother stated Hannah has worried too much.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Mother's comment impact
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is making a fuss to avoid telling her mother the extent of her feelings.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking up at 4 AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at 4 every morning going through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at 4 every morning. I fall asleep fine. Then I'm awake at 4 going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Waking up since term started
facts.content: Hannah has been waking up like this since the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term, I drink a lot of coffee to get through the day, which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: Drinking excessive coffee
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee daily to get through the day.
facts.evidence: Five or six. Then I can't sit still in the afternoons.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water last Thursday.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday, I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.

facts.heading: Feeling exhausted daily
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day from pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day. Just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's advice
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben suggested she should just enjoy her exhaustion.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Feeling guilty and alone
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben suggests she enjoy her feelings.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone. He means well.

facts.heading: Loss of school friends
facts.content: Hannah no longer has friends at school who talk to her.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year 4th quarter with the others.

facts.heading: Line manager role change
facts.content: Hannah became the line manager and this created an awkward situation with former friends.
facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Lost company with promotion
facts.content: Hannah lost some company along with her promotion.
facts.evidence: So you lost some company along with the promotion? Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that.

facts.heading: Missing children and class
facts.content: Hannah misses the children and the daily moments of a child getting something for the first time.
facts.evidence: I miss them. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Current days are spreadsheets
facts.content: Hannah's current days are filled with spreadsheets instead of other activities.
facts.evidence: Now my days are spreadsheets.

facts.heading: Wanted the promotion
facts.content: Hannah thought she wanted the promotion and said yes because she couldn't say no.
facts.evidence: I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Cried after promotion decision
facts.content: Hannah went home and cried after accepting the promotion.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried.

facts.heading: Tears about not returning
facts.content: Hannah's tears were about never getting to go back.
facts.evidence: Tear, I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays when walking in the lakes.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes, and I didn't think about school once for 10 days.

facts.heading: Relaxation during holidays
facts.content: During the holiday, nobody expected anything of Hannah.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me. I was just talking.

facts.heading: Pre-term stress return
facts.content: The week before term, Hannah was a wreck again and could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down good things each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things, a chill laughing, a good email. It helped for about two weeks

facts.heading: Stopped writing due to feeling silly
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing because she felt silly about it.
facts.evidence: and then I stopped because I felt silly. As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook. Noticing what went well is not the same as bragging. It just felt that way.

facts.heading: Goal to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Goal to walk into meeting
facts.content: Hannah wants to walk into a meeting without rehearsing at first.
facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first.

facts.heading: Goal to send email once
facts.content: Hannah wants to send an email only once.
facts.evidence: Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal to rest on Sunday
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa on Sunday evening without anxiety.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feelings after stating goals
facts.content: Hannah felt a light fall, lighter, and a bit tearful when stating her goals.
facts.evidence: A light fall. Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: Telling someone about 4am
facts.content: Hannah has not told anyone how bad her 4am experiences are.
facts.evidence: That's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows how about the 4am.

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah feels scared about telling Ben about her 4am experiences.
facts.evidence: Scary. It would probably be heard that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Plan to tell Ben this week
facts.content: Hannah might try telling Ben this week.
facts.evidence: I might try this week.

facts.heading: Quiet moment for telling
facts.content: Hannah needs a quiet moment to tell Ben.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too warmed up.

facts.heading: Suggesting Saturday morning telling
facts.content: Hannah considered telling Ben on Saturday morning over breakfast.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps? Yeah, over breakfast. He's always in a good mood, Dan.

facts.heading: Try evening notebook again
facts.content: Hannah is considering trying the evening notebook again for one week.
facts.evidence: Would you try the evening notebook again? just for a week. Even one line.
